title: Research Data Series: Index of Common Inflation Expectations

source.name: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System

summary: The Federal Reserve published a FEDS Note introducing the Index of Common Inflation Expectations (CIE), a quarterly research data series that summarizes the comovement of various inflation expectations measures using a dynamic factor model. The March 2021 release contains estimates through 2020Q4, with subsequent quarterly updates scheduled for the third Friday of the first month of each quarter. An updated version of the CIE was introduced in April 2022 with methodological refinements, and the data file was last updated April 17, 2026.
key_points: The CIE uses a dynamic factor model to summarize comovement across multiple inflation expectations measures
The original CIE projected onto SPF (Survey of Professional Forecasters) 10-year PCE inflation and Michigan Survey 5-10 year expectations
April 2022 update added New York Fed Survey of Consumer Expectations measures (1-year and 3-year ahead) and Michigan 25th/75th percentile measures
The 5-year TIPS breakeven inflation measure was removed as redundant with other TIPS data
The original CIE was phased out and replaced by the updated version in the October 2022 release
The series is explicitly experimental and may be discontinued at any time; it is for informational purposes only
why_it_matters: The CIE provides a single summary measure of inflation expectations across multiple surveys and market-based indicators. Market participants and policymakers monitor inflation expectations as a key input for monetary policy decisions and bond market pricing. The experimental nature means users should treat it as supplementary research rather than official Fed guidance.
macro_context: Inflation expectations are a critical input for Fed policy decisions. The CIE aggregates information from SPF, Michigan Survey, and NY Fed SCE to provide a comprehensive view of expected inflation over various horizons. Changes in the CIE could signal shifting inflation dynamics relevant to the Fed's dual mandate.
important_numbers: 2020Q4 (data through this quarter in original release)
2013 (start of New York Fed SCE, explaining why it was not in original index)
AR(5) (autoregressive order of the latent factor in updated model)
